clue.text: Little room for privacy here

parts.note: a small private chamber or cupboard, the sort where one retires to be alone

explanation.definitionFit: A small enclosed cupboard-like room is a classic place to keep things, or oneself, out of sight.

clue.text: A Prime Minister without his patron saints

definitions.text: A Prime Minister without his patron saints

indicators.note: without means the saints' names are taken out of the statesman's full name

parts.note: David Lloyd George, the Welsh Liberal Prime Minister of 1916-22
St David is the patron saint of Wales and St George of England

explanation.surface: A Welsh premier has lost the protection of his saints.
explanation.walkthrough: Take St David (Wales) and St George (England) out of David Lloyd George's full name and his middle name remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle name of the Welsh wartime premier is all that is left once his two saintly names go.

clue.text: But a swan with a pen is no such bird

definitions.text: But a swan with a pen is no such bird

parts.words: But a swan with a pen is no such bird
parts.note: a pen is a female swan, but an office worker with a pen is also the name of a long-legged African raptor

explanation.surface: A swan paired with a female is not that sort of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, so a swan with a pen sounds like a couple; but the office worker holding a pen gives a bird's name, the African snake-hunting raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-legged African bird of prey is named for its crest of quill-like feathers, like pens behind a clerk's ear.

clue.text: Steals fabricated tuft of thread

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up, so these letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief invents a story about tufts of thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' rearranges STEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative bunch of threads tied at one end hangs from cushions and curtains.

clue.text: Slice of UK cheese

definitions.meaning: a county is a slice of the United Kingdom's map
a crumbly English cheese named after its county

explanation.surface: A piece of British cheese cut off the block.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an English county in the north-west and the crumbly cheese named after that county.

clue.text: What are you doing, getting angry with a rebus?

parts.note: to be cross is to be annoyed
a rebus is a word puzzle in pictures or letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks a frustrated solver what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition addresses the reader: what you are doing right now is solving this very thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver reading this clue is at that moment working on a grid of cryptic clues.

clue.text: Kipling's thick-skinned gentleman

parts.note: Kipling's Just So Stories tell how the pachyderm got its trunk

explanation.surface: An insensitive man from a Kipling story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick-skinned' suggests an insensitive person, but it is a pachyderm, the subject of Kipling's Just So story about a curious child getting a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is literally thick-skinned, and Kipling's story features one.

clue.text: Time with one nymph in Paradise

parts.note: an hour is a measure of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spell spent with a beautiful spirit in heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition the faithful are promised beautiful maidens in the gardens of heaven.

clue.text: They're winged and bloody from the knee down

definitions.meaning: wading birds with long red legs
legs coloured blood-red below the knee

explanation.surface: Injured creatures with blood on their lower legs.
explanation.definitionFit: These waders are named for their scarlet legs, and a shank is the leg below the knee.

clue.text: Arden's gold standard ?

parts.note: the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It, set in the Forest of Arden, shares his name with a stone used to assay gold

explanation.surface: A forest's own measure of what counts as precious.
explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It the jester who follows the exiles into the Forest of Arden bears the name of the black stone once rubbed against gold to test its purity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark assaying stone was the old test of gold's purity, hence any standard of judgement; it is also the name of Shakespeare's fool.

clue.text: Free countries get-together

parts.note: the United Nations, the world's countries united, abbreviates to UN
a do is a party or social gathering

explanation.surface: Nations meet for a gathering with no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a knot or fastening is to unfasten it.

clue.text: Nothing doing here on the monster's part ?

definitions.text: Nothing doing here on the monster's part ?

parts.words: Nothing doing here on the monster's part ?
parts.note: inactivity, read as '...', the loch whose famous monster never shows itself

explanation.surface: The Loch Ness monster has yet again failed to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IDLE NESS: the loch where the monster is supposed to live, with nothing doing; the whole word means inactivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing is sloth or inactivity.

clue.text: Stature of the Southend crew

indicators.note: as spoken in Southend, an Essex seaside town where speakers drop the H, so the H word is heard without it

parts.note: a rowing eight is a boat's crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: How tall the rowers from the Essex seaside are.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is an Essex town whose local accent drops the initial H, so a rowing crew, an eight, is how a Southender says the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's tallness.

clue.text: Gull sends other birds back

indicators.note: with 'back', sends the following word back to front
sending back means the word for the birds is read from its end

parts.note: auks are seabirds such as the razorbill and puffin

explanation.surface: A gull drives away other seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends ... back' reverses AUKS.
explanation.definitionFit: This brown predatory seabird is a large gull-like species that harries other birds.

clue.text: Tricks get snake back inside carrier bags

indicators.note: inside means the reversed snake goes within the word for tricks

parts.note: knacks are skilful tricks or techniques

indicators.note: back means the snake's name is read from end to start

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Clever skills bring a serpent back into shopping bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ASP into PSA, which goes 'inside' KNACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rucksacks for hiking are bags for carrying gear on the back.

clue.text: Manner to set up for decoration

indicators.note: to set something up is to arrange it, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A way of arranging things for the sake of decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' rearranges MANNER TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket or adornment is a decoration.

clue.text: How one would be served at 70, Simmery Axe

definitions.text: How one would be served at 70, Simmery Axe

parts.words: How one would be served at 70, Simmery Axe
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Sorcerer, John Wellington Wells, dealer in magic and spells, trades at No 70 Simmery Axe

explanation.surface: A question about service at a London address.
explanation.walkthrough: Simmery Axe is the Cockney form of St Mary Axe, a City of London street; Gilbert and Sullivan's sorcerer John Wellington Wells keeps his shop there.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer's shop would serve its customers by spells and wizardry.

clue.text: Sort of crab I eat could make me ill

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A crab I have eaten might give me food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges CRAB I EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs are microbes that can bring on illness.

clue.text: Pretty maids all in a row in this state ?

definitions.text: Pretty maids all in a row in this state ?

parts.words: Pretty maids all in a row in this state ?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' ends with pretty maids all in a row, so they are on Mary's land, a US state

explanation.surface: A line of pretty girls in some condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's garden belongs to Mary, so it is Mary land; 'state' looks like a condition but is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on Chesapeake Bay is named after Queen Henrietta Maria.

clue.text: Tugs into the wind

indicators.note: the word is turned into another arrangement of its own letters

explanation.surface: A boat tows into a headwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' rearranges TUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a sudden blast of wind.

clue.text: Winding up in flight perhaps

definitions.meaning: coiling round and round as it rises
a flight of stairs may twist round a central column

explanation.surface: Climbing in loops while airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil is a winding course, and a staircase flight can take that twisting form.

clue.text: OK by HM

parts.note: HM is Her Majesty; the monarch's formal approval turns a bill into an Act of Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: The Royal version of this word is the sovereign's formal agreement, the OK given to a bill.

clue.text: One more for shooting?

definitions.meaning: a film walk-on employed for crowd scenes during shooting

explanation.surface: A request for another turn at the shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an additional item, and a non-speaking film actor hired for a shoot.

clue.text: Started to settle in, having been made a lone wolf?

definitions.meaning: taken one's things out of the suitcases on arrival

definitions.text: having been made a lone wolf?

explanation.surface: A newcomer got settled after being cast out of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as UN-PACKED: a wolf thrown out of its pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptying one's luggage is what one does to settle in; a wolf with no pack has been put out of it.

clue.text: The stop-light that is up is down

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: red is the stop signal on a traffic light
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: The traffic signal that has risen has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RED + IE together, giving the duck.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea duck supplies the soft breast feathers that fill quilts, so it stands for down.

clue.text: The end of the bunny girl ?

definitions.text: The end of the bunny girl ?

parts.words: The end of the bunny girl ?
parts.note: a rabbit's short tail, and the fluffy tail worn on a Playboy bunny girl's costume

explanation.surface: The finish of a nightclub hostess's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' seems to mean finish, but it is the rear: a rabbit's short tail, worn as a pompom by a Playboy bunny girl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the short upright tail of a rabbit or deer.

clue.text: Sharp operator against cut-throat competition

parts.note: a keen-edged shaving tool, in competition with the old cut-throat razor

explanation.surface: A shrewd businessman takes on ruthless rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp operator' sounds like a shrewd dealer and 'cut-throat competition' like ruthless trade, but the cut-throat is an open razor, rival of the safety-razor's insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin steel edge fitted into a safety razor is a literally sharp working tool.

clue.text: Adventurous play deploying the spade ace

indicators.note: deploying troops spreads them into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold card game led by laying the ace of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deploying' rearranges SPADE ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring, mischievous adventure is a prank or caper.

clue.text: Money — troubled years for depositors

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

indicators.note: troubled years are disturbed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bank's savers have had a hard time with their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges YEARS after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens that lay eggs deposit them, and strata deposit in beds.
